caption: The drawing depicts a single, centrally placed object that resembles a lantern or lamp. The main body of the lantern is spherical and transparent, rendered in light gray pencil or ink shading to convey the glass surface. The top and bottom metal bands encircling the sphere are decorated with a pattern of small star-shaped cutouts; these bands are shaded in gray hues. At the top of the lantern, a conical metallic structure is attached, also adorned with star-shaped motifs; above this is a large oval-shaped handle, depicted in the same metallic gray tone, with a hinge mechanism attaching it to the top. The bottom section of the lantern is cylindrical with a matching star motif, and within the glass sphere, there appears to be a small central fixture or base, likely representing the area where a candle or fuel reservoir would be positioned. The background is a plain, uncolored parchment or off-white shade, and the drawing is executed in a realistic style with subtle gradations of gray and black for shading and detail. The artist's signature, “ED J. GILGESLEDER,” is inscribed in small, light letters at the bottom right corner of the drawing.
title: Lantern
cluster: #16 — Lighting Devices: Lamps, Lanterns, and Candleholders
